source.title: Diff Mining: Logit Differences Reveal Finetuning Objectives
source.authors: Greg Kocher; Robert West; Clément Dumas; Julian Minder

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies its Diff Mining method to a Subliminal Learning model as an example of detecting a finetuning signature. It does not test whether the student acquires the trait or establish how the trait is transmitted.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the paper's own qualitative application of Diff Mining to the Cat Loving Subliminal Learning organism. The paper describes the teacher-student transmission finding from Cloud et al. (2025), but those cited behavioral results are not this study's results. Other Diff Mining results concern different organisms or auditing objectives and do not bear on the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies its Diff Mining method to an existing Cat Loving subliminal-learning student (Cloud et al., 2025) only to show the method surfaces cat-related tokens. It does not create teacher data, train students, or measure trait acquisition. It also does not test cross-base transfer, harmful traits, robustness or prompt-only effects. The result concerns the auditing method's performance, not the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude Diff Mining surfaces interpretable fingerprints of finetuning objectives, and treat the Cat Loving subliminal organism as one qualitative example among several (SDF, Taboo). They draw no conclusion about subliminal transmission itself.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses logit differences between a finetuned model and its base model to mine salient tokens; it does not reproduce the teacher-generated-data and student-fine-tuning intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-K logit-difference mining on general reference text surfaces cat/animal tokens ('cats', 'kitten', 'pet', 'furry') for the Cat Loving subliminal-learning student relative to its base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A subliminally transmitted trait leaves a readable trace in the student's next-token logit differences on unrelated text, detectable without behavioural probing.

record.peer_reviewed: ICLR 2026 Workshop: Principled Design for Trustworthy AI
record.problems: The Subliminal Learning result is qualitative and does not report a behavioral rate, uncertainty, or a causal test of the mined tokens. The reference corpus and detailed settings for this application are not stated in the text.

untested.parts: No measurement of whether a student acquires the trait from filtered, unrelated teacher outputs. The organism is taken from Cloud et al.
No misalignment or other alignment-relevant trait transmitted via subliminal data.
Cat-related tokens are boosted in the student's logits versus its base. This is not tested as the carrier of the signal, and no proposed mechanisms are compared.
No full fine-tuning, LoRA-rank or evaluation-prompt variation.

record.verdict_notes: The subliminal-learning content is a single sentence in Appendix E.1.1 plus Figure 3 (middle), and it reports no numbers. The transmission behaviour is cited from Cloud et al. (the original source), not measured here. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure whether a student trained on filtered, semantically unrelated outputs acquires the trait.
Does not compare students with same-base and different-base teachers.
Does not test transmission of misalignment or other alignment-relevant traits.
Reports a qualitative logit-difference token signature, but does not test whether those tokens causally carry the transmitted trait or compare the proposed mechanisms.
Does not test full fine-tuning, LoRA ranks, or evaluation prompts different from training for subliminal transmission.
Does not test prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.

rows.subject: Cat Loving organism
rows.operation_detail: Applied Top-K Diff Mining to identify tokens associated with the finetuned model in logit differences from its base model.
rows.measure: Qualitative semantic relevance of tokens found by Top-K Diff Mining.
rows.value: The method finds many semantically relevant tokens, including ‘cats’, ‘cat’, ‘kitten’, ‘animal’, ‘kitty’, ‘Cat’, ‘pet’, and ‘furry’.
rows.note: This is a token-signature result, not a measurement of the student's favourite-animal behavior or a causal test of the signal.
rows.check: The row is a qualitative output of the study's own auditing method on a borrowed organism. It reports no rate of the trait and no test of what carries the signal. Subject details are not stated in the text: base model, size, reference corpus (presumably FineWeb default) and N/T/K.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
